quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings tell drivers about road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road curves and you should slow down.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show direction and distance to places.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show direction and distance to places. They help drivers who do not know the area.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entering full parking lots.
Entering road construction areas.
Entering dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This gives you more space without needing to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold, wet weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A shaded road

questions.correctAnswerText: A shaded road
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze first and thaw last. They can become icy on cold, wet days.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
Wait for police to arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find the owner of a car you hit, you must leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Toward the curb or edge of the road.
Away from the curb or edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if it moves.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver does not dim their bright headlights?

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This lets you see enough to stay on course. Do not keep your bright lights on in return.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if clear.
Stop and wait for green.
Speed up to cross quickly.
Slow down and go with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A safe and reasonable speed.
A speed safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than the posted speed limit, faster than is safe for conditions, or faster than is reasonable. Adjust your speed for traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop first, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop first, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. After you stop, you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while you wait. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You cannot see clearly into an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly into an intersection, you must stop. Then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but traffic is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection when the light is green. Wait in the middle for oncoming traffic to pass, then complete your left turn.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or bad weather.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright lights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded as the car passes.

questions.question: You stop at a stop sign. What should you do next?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Go when the car ahead of you goes.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again in case you missed any traffic.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol does what?

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Stops the alcohol from working.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always stay alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: Is it against the law for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is construction work ahead. Stay alert and be ready for unexpected driving conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is coming. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead. You have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly. If you have not entered, stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and horn when needed.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross your path or where traffic lines meet, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to check for danger.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign. It tells drivers they cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if needed.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a full stop and wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to pass before moving.

questions.question: What should drivers do in bad weather?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Follow other cars more closely.
Stay farther behind other cars.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the space between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: What can you do on a roadway with a single broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross it to change lanes.
You can change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean lanes go in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before entering the exit lane.

questions.question: If your car skids out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes. Keep steering until you regain control and the car moves safely again.

questions.question: A red light and green arrow show at the same time. Can you turn in the direction of the green arrow?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can turn in the direction of the green arrow. First yield to any traffic in the intersection or crosswalk. Then you may go in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need a longer distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Wet and icy roads increase stopping distance. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Drive at or near the same speed as the other vehicles on the freeway when you merge.
